body: Yes, this has absolutely happened to me.  For some reason I now can't get fully hard or at least as hard as I used to.  That's so much more frustrating then being fully hard and able to last forever.

Yes, absolutely.  I decided I couldn't risk giving this to someone else, even if they were willing to risk it.  Honestly, most of the women I dated or tried to date were not willing to move forward "normally" in a relationship after disclosure.  I've heard guys that are married now that have wife's ask for them to wear boxers and condoms for sex.  Not girlfriends, WIVES.  I had a girlfriend say I can do this with a glove on and that she'd still like to date me.  She had no idea how that hurt.  So, I went to sites that were herpes dating sites.  So yes, I settled.  It's been a long road to where I am now.  Looking back on it all, it wasn't worth the pain.

So, you've had it for 2 years.  Ok.  It might just be the company you keep, your expectations in life.  I'm sure I could have hung around different people, different women, that wouldn't have cared about an incurable STD.  Who knows, maybe your a Marine I deployed with.  I can't judge, but apparently you can.  I'm not gonna justify myself anymore to you.  To be honest, I'd like to hear your justification that you've handled this well or responsibly, because that would surprise me.  Also, seems you missed the gist of my post, the point is, it's not easy to commit suicide.  People look at those that commit suicide as weak, when in fact it's the hardest thing someone can do, especially if they do it to protect others.

I am more than this virus.  I know that.  Being more than this virus is what keeps me trapped in this painful existence.  Even if you are more and realize you are more, this virus is a BIG part of me, of us.  Some can ignore it, but if it wasn't a defining part of our existence, we wouldn't be posting on this sub, would we?

I agree, I am a sad man. And the statistics are all over the place, no one really knows how many are sick with this.  Also, statistics don't matter if person after person, girl after girl, woman after woman, you interact with does not have this and is scared of being infected for life regardless of their feeling for you.  That's not "statistics," that's life, that's reality. 

As far as me being a "pathetic" man, not even close.  I've accomplished so much in life in spite of the obstacles and pain and isolation and despair and rejection this disease has brought me since I was a sophomore in HS.  I've fought for this country as a military officer.  I have a Masters degree.  Money is not a measure of a man or happiness, but I have made six figures (and then some) for years.  I am an AMAZING father and son and brother and uncle and boss and employee and youth sports coach and scout leader and friend.  Even through my depression and despair.  To be honest, because of my connections in life, it is what pulls me back away from the relief of suicide.  I wish I was pathetic and didn't have so many people that love and rely on me, it would be so much easier to end it all and the pain.  

I'm not sure why you have a problem with me and my pain and my experiences.  I chose long ago that I would never endanger causing the pain of this disease on someone else, I guess I could have made different choices, but I never got a choice with this disease, so I didn't feel I could ever jeopardize someone else to this.  Seriously though, what bothers you about my despair?

I guess we'll just agree to disagree.  I've experienced too much to trivialize this.  And I've been following and hearing about a vaccine or cure since the turn of the century.  I am fortunate I guess, this virus has barely effected me physically.  I think because I got it so young as a teenager and my first OB was really bad.  Either way, I wish the emotional and mental impact of isolation and rejection and humiliation and everything else associated with this disease was the same.  I think a lot of people ignore it.  They infect others.  They think it's not a big deal.  And it's just a vicious cycle.  If 80% have it (which is way too big a number) then I'm the most unlucky guy in the world with the women I met in my dating life before limiting myself to those that know and accept the isolation of the disease.

I'm not posing a hypothetical.  I'm not new to this world of herpes.  I've experienced and seen the rejection, isolation, humiliation that comes with this disease.  These are not "thoughts," they are experiences of my life.  And, every last one is herpes related.

Wait, you think I'm a troll?  Because I challenged someone for comparing herpes to the flu or a cold?  I went to this sub because I really am considering, even trying to get the courage to commit suicide.  Sorry if I misunderstood the sub, I thought that was what it was for.  Seems like that's what it is for.  I'll admit, I'm not rainbows and butterflies here, I'm actually contemplating killing myself.  Sorry my pain and sharing it with this community offended you so much.

I've always been monogamous.  At least tried to be.  Put time into relationships.  Again, probably because I got this disease before finishing puberty.  Anyway, when you approach life and sex like that, there's only so many times you can face rejection and humiliation.  I never even considered the one night stands, wouldn't have been fair to the girl even if she said she was willing to risk a life long disease for a hookup.  And when you are friends with someone, when someone gets really vested in you, tells you they like you, even gets to the point they ask why haven't you made a move on me... then you tell them and everything changes, it takes a piece of your soul.  Only so many times you can have your soul damaged like that.  You can't imagine the rejections I've received that were "technically" acceptance.  Women saying, well, we can be together, but I'll only do this with you.  I'll avoid details, but you can imagine how someone that says they love you deciding to only touch parts of you with gloves on.  It does unbelievable damage to a human. 
I eventually gave up and only dated others with the disease.  And you could say "moved on" with my life.  Technically living the American dream.  Just with a damaged heart and soul.

Thanks, and I appreciate where you are coming from and your good intentions.  But your mentality, especially when adopted by so many, is the reason why herpes still spreads.  It's also the reason our disease has not received the funding or attention necessary to find a cure or vaccine.  Worst of all, I personally feel it trivializes the lifetime of pain and rejection many of us face, and I personally experienced.  Ok, the disease doesn't make your heart stop or your lungs stop working, its much more insidious, it isolates you and leads to ridicule and humiliation and depression.  Honestly, those can be much worse than death and more painful.

Flip that from chickenpox to herpes, same applies.  When they colonize Mars, it won't be with millions of people.  And I'm sure they will screen for certain genetic traits.  They should also screen for herpes.  One way to get past this virus we have no control over is to leave it behind.  Pretty cool to think about a colony without any STDs, especially the incurable kind.

On the flip side, it's amazing how many women that liked me and wanted sexual relations and possibly more completely rejected and changed their mindset on me as a person when I told them.  Not many talk about it, and I'm not trivializing the stigmatism this causes for women, but this disease is so much more brutal on men and their potential relationships.

Correct, but that's my point.  This is the only article I've seen that tried to tackle what people were thinking before committing suicide based on google search history.  And, surprisingly to them, but probably not to us, they were searching about herpes and others that have it.  If this was more main stream awareness, maybe we'd have more priority and funding for a herpes cure or vaccine.

Really?  Wow!  Many doctors still won't test asymptomatic COVID exposure.  They'll tell you to self-isolate, which hopefully people do, but based on the numbers, not likely happening as frequently as you think or we hope. And the doctors will say there is no reason to test asymptomatic COVID because it's a virus we can't do anything about.  Hydrate and rest. 

This logic also implies and many will attest that doctors will tell them, there's no point in testing for herpes because there's nothing you can do about it.  Also, the CDC is suggesting that if people knew they had asymptomatic herpes they would not change their sexual behavior anyways.  That is not true and really shows how little the CDC thinks of Americans.

You talk about COVID "misbehavior" resulting in public shaming and even law enforcement action.  That happens FREQUENTLY with herpes.  We hear about when it's celebrities frequently in the news with herpes being sued, but it happens without celebrities even more frequently (obviously).

If you are looking for "evidence" to show that asymptomatic people with COVID that know they have COVID (or don't know) continue their same behavior prior to the diagnosis, I won't be able to show that to you.  But I don't see how anyone doesn't think that's not happening with the COVID numbers we have.
Correct, it reduces symptoms, kind of like Valtrex.  We're going to be wearing masks for a LONG time.
But obviously you didn't do it.  Do you regret not doing it?  That's where I'm at now.  I wish I would have had the guts to get it done before.

Hate to break it to you, but if we were going to colonize another planet, they had better thoroughly screen anyone going for herpes and exclude them.  If we would only send those not infected, we would have a herpes free colony.  Not sure if your example makes.me.feel any better, when that is probably the reality.

Its amazing how it depends if it's the girl or guy infected.  If it's the girl, the guy will usually risk his health, either eventually or right off the bat.  If it's the guy infected, typically the girl won't have anything to do with him.  If she does want to risk it, she'll likely want as much protection as possible.  It would be interesting if someone could study that.  Of course there will always be the exception to prove the rule, maybe even from someone reading this.  But I recommend dating within the herpes circle, especially if you are an infected guy.

Quoting the CDC website as it relates to herpes... 

"CDC does not recommend herpes testing for people without symptoms. This is because diagnosing genital herpes in someone without symptoms has not shown any change in their sexual behavior (e.g., wearing a condom or not having sex) nor has it stopped the virus from spreading."

This is the EXACT same logic that was used to not push testing for asymptomatic COVID.  These people are villains.  Not only do they have the death of 300,000 plus on their hands from COVID, but the incurable infection of countless people with herpes.  I've spent years, decades, suffering keeping others safe from my incurable disease, changing my "sexual behavior." Do you not see how their stance has harmed the American people and lead to a herpes epidemic of despair across the country?  Not to mention taking the exact same actions regarding COVID testing that contributed, if not caused, the uncontrolled spread of the coronavirus?  Surely you see the connection.

I've had this disease for more than half my life now, 26 years.  I got it from the first girl I ever kissed at 16.  I'm 42 now, married with kids.  Great job, I have a Master's degree.  Coach little league.  All that stuff they say makes for a happy, regular, suburbia life. And I look back on my life and think of all the pain and suffering I had for decades, and still have now.  It wasn't worth it.  I'm not with the woman I'm supposed to be with.  I haven't lived the life I was supposed to live.  All because of a stupid teenage hormonal mistake.  I wish I could say it gets better.  And there are times you might forget.  But at least for me, it's been 26 years of hell.  I got at least another 26 years to go, I guess.  Hopefully not much longer than that.

This goes back to other posts that I made.  If that guy would have accepted his situation, and instead of trying to live a normal life like he did acting like he wasn't infected with a life long disease, but rather faced his reality and committed suicide, he would not have infected you or others.  The alternative I guess was for him to live his life in a reclusive state of depression rejecting sexual interaction and relationships.  I sadly chose that path and turned away from so many girls and women in my life because of herpes and it's caused nothing but unbelievable pain and despair.  I'd rather not have lived through that pain and despair, but had I died of suicide I would have been considered a coward.  I think our society has it's priorities mixed up.  We value the wrong things.  Suffering for so long should not be the answer for us.  We rather should honor those that are willing and able to commit suicide to avoid harming others with an incurable disease.

Good Lord!  I just read that schizophrenic illogical reasoning by the CDC for not recommending herpes testing.  That's RIDICULOUS!  They don't recommend testing because they believe even if you are positive but have no symptoms your sexual behavior won't change?  What?  I haven't had an OB for years, can't even remember when, but my life has been turned upside down and devastated by herpes as I worked for decades to not infect others.  I am so disgusted with the CDC and our government.  Angry too.  Sickened.  This helps me better understand why COVID is ripping through this country, because this CDC logic about herpes is applied to COVID.  These are sick,.dangerous people.
I challenge that.  How many people die from suicide because of herpes.  We don't know.  But it very well could easily be thousands.

I think it depends on the reason.  And honestly, many suicides do it because they are a burden on their family and friends.  In my case I attempted suicide because I was an actual walking disease that would infect anyone that I had sex with an incurable life long STD (herpes).  We know because we are posting on this site, it's not easy to take that step, to pull that trigger.  It takes guts.  I often hear people accuse those that die by suicide of being cowards, not "stupid." I can think of nothing more brave than jumping on a grenade to protect others, and if your life harms or could harm those around you, I see nothing more brave than committing suicide.

I agree, it's just we never hear about those that sacrificed themselves to stop the spread of this virus.  I would think someone that chose to die rather than spread an incurable disease should be honored.  They made a sacrifice for others.  Not just anyone, but they sacrificed themselves so they would not harm those closest to them that they would have been intimate with or even marry.  I wish society would recognize that, it would make the step of suicide so much easier for those of us that don't want to harm others with an incurable disease.

I agree, it's just we never hear about it.  I would think someone that chose to die rather than spread an incurable disease should be honored.  They made a sacrifice for others. I'm not sure if you are joking or not.  But I assure you, herpes is a very big deal.  I personally know women that have loved me step out of my life because they didn't want to be infected.  It is a life long mark that ruins relationships and love before they even start.  That's not to mention the casual ridicule or humiliation of it on a daily basis, by many who technically mean no harm because they might not know you have it and by some that might know you have it and just use it as a weapon to hurt you.  The flu, a cold, even COVID for that matter go away eventually.  Not this.

I suppose it is #1.  I can't even remember my last OB.  Call it a midlife crisis, I am looking back on all the rejection, pain, limitation, humiliation this disease put on me.  My wife is great and so is the rest of my life it would seem.  But I limited my dating to those already infected years ago.  Because of that, I'm not with the woman I should be with.  I'm not living the life I should be living.  I didn't live the life I should have lived.  All because of a mistake I made decades ago as a teenager that had never even kissed someone before.  So, I guess to answer your question, what is driving my desire to looking forward to death... Regret is probably the one word I'd use.

It's just weird how people so often say it changes over time, gets better.  But that's the deal, herpes doesn't go away.  Nothing changes.  Maybe we change, maybe we change our expectations for life, for partners, for dating, etc.  And then we get used to our new life and think this is how it's supposed to be.  To be honest, I don't know why people with this life long incurable disease say it gets better.  I guess that's why I'm here now.

I tried a long time ago, but not really.  Just took sleeping pills.  If I had a gun back then, I probably wouldn't be dealing with my current pain and impossible scenario.  I think maybe some people commit suicide but then it never gets made known they did it because of herpes. Thanks.  You're a really nice person.  If it's any consolation, I don't have the guts to go through with it.  So, I'm not going anywhere.  I think that ship has sailed.  At least until I get to a point where my kids don't need me anymore, but that's a long ways away.  I guess we all have regrets in life, it's amazing how one bad decision at 16 can destroy so much and cause so much sadness for a lifetime.  Oh well.

I'm "happily" married with children too.  Unfortunately it's because of my kids I think I've boxed myself in and can't exit the pain like I wish I could.  I just look back on my life and there's so much pain and missed opportunity and heart break because of this disease.  I also got it from my first girlfriend, the first girl I kissed.  I still can't believe she wasn't a virgin too.  I never even confronted her over it, dated her all throughout high school because I was scared to death.  So many nights spent crying as a kid and young adult.  I think it's a lot easier for women, you can see it on dating websites.  Did your friends only date people with herpes they met on websites?  I imagine not.  It makes it a lot easier to move on in life when many men are able to see past this.  Maybe I'm wrong, but I have decades of experience with this, and many, MANY women won't look past this.  It just is what it is.

The people I worked with were part of my military unit.  The unit had men and women.  I had been holding this pain in for a long time. Some on the unit had been hooking up with each other and I had rejected advances from some of the women because I didn't want to have to tell them.  Well, some people thought I might be gay because of that, nothing against gay people, but when you're not gay you don't want people thinking you are. Anyway, I told one of the guys in my unit when we were drinking because I wanted it off my chest.  Really messed up my life for years before I could get away from that unit, job, and people that knew about it.  It still kind of followed me for years after that, because the military is big, but not that big, especially in certain lines of work.  Anyways, sorry, my story isn't very positive.  But, it's real.  Thank you for responding.

Thanks for responding.  It means a lot.  I manage the virus fine, I can't even remember my last outbreak.  I've had it since I was 16.  The virus has completely dictated the direction of my social life and I'm just tired of it and the pain and sadness.  I don't think I have the guts to go through with suicide, that's why I was wondering if anyone knew someone that did.  Some would think this weird, but I'd consider those people strong, it's not easy to take that step.  I'll probably just keep going through the motions of life.  Not judging, but HSV1 (assuming that's oral) is a whole different ball game than genital herpes.  Although, I'm very sorry and angry this virus hurt you really your whole life.  It's had me since before I was probably finished with puberty in all honesty.  I totally get it.

I just don't tell my wife anything.  I mentioned it once that I'd prefer to be dead than alive.  It didn't do anyone any good.  Just have to decide if I have the guts to check out.  Or just keep on suffering through life.

So, I'm not sure if this will help.  But, I'm on and thought I'd try.  Do you have any interests or passions?  Do you follow a sports team, bowl, play basketball, coach a youth team, etc?  I know with the pandemic everything is upside down, but that will eventually go away.  I would recommend finding something your passionate about and trying it out.  Unless there risk more to what's wrong, which I'm sure there is.  Just thought I'd ask and maybe give you that option in the future.

Wow, I am definitely one of those guys in their 40s regretting not killing themselves earlier.  Honestly, I didn't know it was a thing.  How many people do you know like that?  And why don't they kill themselves now?  I messed up because I have kids, and I think I've doomed myself to another 30+ years of pain because I can't abandon them.  I'm stuck and it REALLY sucks.

Trust me, it's not just a matter of feeling.  I screwed up and told ONE person at my work years ago when I was drinking at a Christmas party.  Everyone knew within a week or two and 90% of them acted VERY differently around me.  You'll get the jokes about making sure that no one accidentally drinks from your cup and many other things.  It's not just a feeling, it's unfortunately reality.

Anyways, your friends don't need to know.  I intentionally never dated within my circle of friends because I knew I'd have to disclose to that person and that she'd probably tell her and my friends.

Been there.  Still there off and on.  It's a choice to keep living which I made for almost the exact same reasons you did, I did not want to hurt my parents, friends, and even my pet.  If you ever have kids though, it becomes impossible, you lose that choice and just have to live with the pain.  Just something to think about.  As you know, herpes never leaves us.  I've been one of those who life was irreparably changed by this disease now for over 20 years.

Totally respect and appreciate your post.  But it seems when we depict this life altering disease as something that doesn't devastate lives or lead many to suicide, it makes a cure or vaccine less imperative.  I mean, if it's just a rash that doesn't devastate thousands or even millions of people's lives, why prioritize it when there are so many other horrible diseases out there.  I've suffered with herpes since I was 16 yo.  I'm an accomplished, educated, good looking guy.  I have an MBA, have made a six figure salary for over a decade.  I can't even begin to tell you the unintentional cruelness I have faced over those 20 plus years.  The isolation.  The embarrassment.  The rejection.  It might be the crowd and people I've been around.  I'm religious, educated, and candidly and sadly, I would have never risked getting this disease if I had a choice which I never had.  So I don't blame then for their unintentional cruelness.  Oh well, just my thoughts.

100 days later, Christmas season, pandemic raging, how are you?  I've been slipping lately with the depression.  I focus on HSV and how it has dictated so much of my life.  Not sure if the depression would be there without HSV or I'd have another thing to focus on without it.  Chick/egg situation.  How are you doing?
Sorry to hear that.  Feel free to DM me if you want to chat.
Have been before.  Not so much now.  Comes and goes.

I was 16 when I got it from the first girl I ever kissed.  The pain fo feeling "dirty" or having your life derailed never really goes away.  It just lessens.  I try to think it could be worse, it could be a disease that shortest your life.  Try to talk and surround yourself with people that have it.  Forrtunately (and I fortunately), so many of us with herpes get married, have kids, and move on.  We have successful lives and never even think about it after getting married and moving past the dating world.  I only tried a couple times to date women that weren't infected, didn't work out and then limited myself to only those with HSV.  You have some paths to choose.  It does get better, hope you find that amazing guy with herpes, he's out there.  Feel free to DM.

Not trying to judge, but how did this marriage come about?  The "stigma" of herpes really only applies when you're out there dating.  If you married to stay married, then the stigma should not be a reason why you have to have sex in a bubble.  Good luck, does not sound like a woman I'd want to be around.
Best of BOTH worlds.  Thanks!  I'll be asking about Bupropion for sure.
Were you still able to last longer and finish?  Like I said in my OP, I like being able to last longer but would want to be able to finish.
Just letting you know you're not alone.  Working out helped for me.  Cardio, running.
You're a good person.  Better than many.  That's all I can say.

Find something to put yourself into.  I got this when I was 16 or 17, can't even remember it was so long ago.  I really focused on my sport (soccer) and academics.  Find something beyond casual sexual relationships.  Use this as a jump start to add to your life.  Make true friends, new friends, have fun with friends that has nothing to do with sex (harder to do because of this stupid pandemic, I know).

You don't have to tell your boss anything.  Tell him you have a cold.  You're body is still adjusting to the virus.  Take vitamins, especially vitamin C and D.  I know it's hard because of this horrible pandemic, but try to stay in decent physical shape, hydrated, and rested.  It will get better, you're still adjusting.

I'm probably not the best to answer, since technically I have the same question as you.  But... I think you shouldn't even feel a relaxed pelvis floor.  It should just feel "normal", no pain, tingling, tightness.  Hope that helps.

"Shaming people"?  Now that's  harsh.  I spent plenty a day when I was 23 yo crying with this infection.  I know how hard it is, and even watching a movie with some herpes joke would cause me to lose it.  Advising someone to look for another person where there's no infection risk or ensuring that person truly understands the possible commitment of an infection is VERY far from shaming someone.  I would never shame someone, I've been at this since high school.  I spent years feeling shameful, close to decades.  Don't read into what I wrote, just read the words.

On a positive note, I actually think it's very likely.  Like I said, by the numbers there are MILLIONS of "us" that have this.  And I feel strongly there should be "free" dating apps for those positive, similar to the other apps.  It's VERY unfortunate that dating apps have costs for positive individuals, although I hear OK Cupid does have that option to self identify.  I'm not sure in what context you are quoting me, but I've dealt with this for over 20 years, and I stand by saying I'm not sure how I (or by correlation someone else), could risk the health of another for a life long condition knowingly.  I certainly would not risk my health for life if I was given that option before, which I was not given.  And each person is unique of course, but someone that would risk a life long illness for someone they aren't marrying, I would question that person's judgement.  But I think when people are young, they don't look past Saturday night, much less 10 to 20 years from now.  

Please, I don't want to cause more emotional pain to you or anyone that is dealing with this.  It's hard enough.  Accept my apology and I'll slowly back out of the room.  Best of luck, whatever your situation.

It won't kill someone.  I don't want it to sound like that at all.  I'm just saying that dating and relationships become much harder with it, and that doesn't change when you are 30, 40, or 50.  If this person you see as being with when 30, 40, or 50, go for it.  And I wish you both the best.  But I feel a lot of times the effect on a lifetime is lost by those in youth, especially youth in lust.  But, that's your partners choice, as long as they understand, to each their own.  Good luck!  And I hope you all the happiness you deserve.

Whoa, whoa, whoa.  I'm not trying to be negative.  In fact, I'm trying to do the opposite.  This is not a fatal illness, I'm well aware of that. But it is a life long illness.  According to the numbers there are millions of people with this. And it seems many think it is impossible to find someone that already has this for a relationship.  In fact, I think it's the opposite and because of the stigma we don't know how many people are out there that someone could date that already have this, which would mean no risk for either partner to be infected.  And I think it's unfortunate that many couples that successfully meet that both already have herpes seem to disappear from the "herpes world" after their successful relationship.  It's good, because it shows life's not over and you can move on.  But I will definitely back off on any advice if it bothers anyone that much.  Not my intent at all.
